findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a certified food protection manager present at the start of the inspection. Discussed with PIC. The owner arrived shortly throughout the inspection, which he is the only person who is food manager certified. Violation corrected. Ensure that there is always a person who is food manager certified on site at all times if serving food.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was a dead fly observed inside of a container of broth within the walk in cooler. The broth was stored uncovered. Shown to the PIC and the broth was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are covered during storage to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The settings were altered on the machine during the visit and the machine was retested at 100ppm (CL). Violation corrected. Ensure that the dish machine tests at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed with a SIGNIFICANT amount of mold on the food contact surfaces:
- baffle of the ice machine
- nozzles of the soda machine
Shown to the PIC and the soda nozzles were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection, however, a follow-up will be scheduled for October 8, 2026 to see that ice baffles have been cleaned and sanitized. Ensure to clean baffles as frequent as often to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed various Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods that lacked proper date marking. These foods included pizza sauces, cooked noodles, sliced deli meats, meatballs, etc. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are date marked if being stored in house longer than 24 hours. Provide a date marking for items with the date that foods are prepared and/or the discard date. Will follow-up on October 8, 2026 to see that foods are date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed rodent droppings on the floor and other surfaces throughout the dish room. There was a five inch gap in the corner behind the dish machine that could act an entry point for rodents. Shown and discussed with the PIC. Ensure that entry points are sealed and that a professional pest management company is contacted to service the facility. Will follow-up on  October 8, 2026 to check on pest activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The food containers inside of the top prep cooler were observed heavily accumulated with food debris. Ensure that containers are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The additional employees that handles food are not food manager, nor food handler certified. Ensure that all employees who handle food or clean dishes are at least food handler certified. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: The inspectors didn’t observe any handwashing during the visit. An employee was observed rinsing hands inside of the hand sink. Discussed that handwashing shall occur frequently and whenever contamination of the hands occur. Most of the handsinks throughout the facility are supplied with running weather, paper towels, and hand soap, with the exception of one sink (see violation #10). Ensure to educate employees on proper handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed at least two employees bare hand cooked pizza during the visit. The activity was ceased and corrected. Ensure to never use bare hands with any ready-to-eat food items. Utensils or single use gloves shall always be used to handle RTE foods to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the men’s restroom to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- the PIC was informed and paper towels were placed. Ensure all sinks intended for hand washing always have warm running water, soap, and paper towels to complete proper handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs stored above cooked meats in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- education was conducted with the PIC and the eggs were moved below the meats. Ensure all raw products are stored below cooked products to prevent potential contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed Italian dressing labeled “refrigerate after opening” stored on the counter next to the salad prep cooler (surface temperature of 72F probed). CORRECTED- the dressing was placed in the cold holding unit. Ensure all temperature control safety (TCS) food items and items labeled “Keep Refrigerated” or “Refrigerate after opening” are held at or below 41F to limit the growth of pathogens that may cause food-borne illness.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility lacks proper date marking for TCS foods in the walk in cooler. These items include but aren’t limited to items containing cooked chicken, pork, pasta sauces, and other various items. Discussed with PIC proper date marking and that TCS foods shall never be held longer than 7 days after preparation. Items were date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that any TCS foods held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed at least five dead insects throughout the facility, these areas included the storage/office space and in the basement area. The owner mentioned that the facility currently doesn’t have pest control and will be getting a new pest control company soon. Discussed that a professional  pest control  company shall provide treatment to the facility to help eliminate the presence of insects. The facility is also expected to clean frequently and prevent harboring conditions for insects. Will follow-up on 5/27/2026 to ensure that the premise is free of insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.comment:
The additional food employees couldn’t show proof of food handler certificates. Discussed with both the employee and the owner that a food certificate is required for any employee that handles food or clean dishes. Ensure that a food handler certificate is obtained by the next routine visit.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Two containers of ground beef were observed in the walk-in cooler at 46F and 48F, probed. Both PIC and a food employee indicated that all foods in the walk-in cooler had been there since yesterday and that no foods prepared today had been placed in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded the out of temperature ground beef. Ensure time/temperature controlled for safety foods are held at 41F or below at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The walk in cooler was observed with an ambient temperature of 45F using inspector’s probe thermometer. Ground beef was observed at 47 and 48F and was voluntarily discarded. Other foods were observed at 42-45F (tomato sauces, pizza dough, broth). PIC stated that the cooler is approximately 40F when he arrives in the morning, but based on inspectors observations the cooler struggles to maintain that temperature when the door is opened frequently during the day. The walk-in cooler needs to be serviced. Inspectors will follow up on 10/15/25 to see that the cooler is maintaining foods at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were several containers of uncovered items in the walk in cooler such as but not limited to meats, tomato sauce, broths, etc. All foods stored in coolers must bear a covering to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

Ensure that the dish machine tests at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility lacks proper date marking for TCS foods in the walk in cooler. These items include but aren’t limited to items containing cooked beef, pasta sauces, cooked noodles, and other various items. Discussed with PIC proper date marking and items were date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that any TCS foods held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: A container of cooked ground beef was dated 9/10/25 in the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC that all TCS foods can only be cold held for up to seven days before needing to be discarded. The PIC mentioned that the meat was prepared two days prior to the inspection. The proper date sticker was added to the container to correct the violation. Ensure that cooked meats are never held in house longer than 7 days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The ambient temperature of the walk in cooler was observed at 45F. Discussed having the walk in cooler serviced due to alarming ambient temperature. Ambient temperatures for cold holding should be 41F or below. PIC mentioned that the door of the cooler had been opened and closed recently, which has caused the cooler to increase in temperature. Ensure that cold holding equipment is capable of maintaining proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow-up on 10/9/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The only allergen certificate available in house has expired (7/2025). Ensure that an allergen certificate is obtained and available by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The bottle of hand soap in the women’s restroom was empty. Discussed with PIC and soap bottle was refilled with liquid soap. Be sure that hand soap is available at every hand-sink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: The meatballs stored in a container in the walk in cooler were observed to be covered with mold. The meatballs were shown to the owner and were discarded. Ensure that meatballs are marked with the day of preparation and are discarded if not used within the 7-day timeframe. Day 1 counts as the day meatballs are prepared. The facility has an additional 6 days to hold the meatballs in house. Discard if meatballs aren't used at the end of day 7.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: A bowl of cut lettuce stored inside of the service cooler was observed uncovered. Also, there were several containers of uncovered items in the walk in cooler such as but not limited to meats, tomato sauce, and broths. All foods stored in coolers must bear a covering to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There were food items stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC that foods must be placed on shelves or at least 6 inches above the floor. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed accumulated debris in several of the coolers throughout the facility. The inner surfaces of the coolers contained dried food debris. Ensure to clean inner surfaces of equipment as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
There weren’t any paper towels in either the men’s or women’s bathroom. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. Ensure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink to properly wash hands.  

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
There wasn’t any hand soap at the hand-sink in the women’s restroom. Discussed with PIC and hand soap was provided. Ensure that hand soap is available at every hand-sink to wash hands properly. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Observed the meatballs in the walk in cooler to be accumulated with mold. Discussed with PIC and meatballs were pulled and discarded. Ensure that meatballs are dated marked and used within 7 days of opening to prevent mold accumulation. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the food contact surface of the can opener to be accumulated with food debris. Discussed with PIC and can opener was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation. 

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the inside baffles of the ice machine to be accumulated with mold. Discussed with PIC and ice baffles were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that ice baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent mold accumulation. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a couple gallons of whole milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date. The use-by-dates were 11/11/2024 and 11/15/2024. Discussed with PIC and milks were pulled from the walk in cooler. Ensure that milks never exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date and are discarded if not used within 7 days of opening.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Several TCS food items stored in the walk in cooler were not date marked such as but not limited to ground beef, meatballs, various kinds of pasta, and pizza sauces. Discussed with PIC that any TCS food stored in house longer than 24 hours will need to be date marked. Ensure to date mark TCS food items stored in house overnight and discard if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a certified food manager present at the facility. The only CFPM wasn’t present during the inspection. Be sure that a CFPM is present at all hours of operation to ensure food safety. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee barehand Ready-to-eat food items including but not limited to deli meat, sliced cheese, and tomatoes. These foods were stored in the salad prep cooler in the front of the house. Inspector ceased activity and instructed the employee to throw away the food items that were barehanded. Ensure that RTE foods are never barehanded and are always handled with gloved hands to protect from contamination. 

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the soap dispenser in the women’s bathroom to not be functioning properly. Soap wasn't able to dispense. PIC corrected the violation by providing a bottle of hand soap. Be sure that hand soap is available at every hand-sink to ensure hands are getting washed properly.  

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed several food items including but not limited to sausage (ground & whole), meatballs, and various sauces to be uncovered in the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC that food items will need to be covered during storage. Ensure that all stored foods are covered to protect against contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed two gallons of whole milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date. The use-by-date was July 14, 2024. PIC discarded the gallons of milk. Ensure that milks never exceed the manufactured use-by-date and are discarded if not used within 7 days of opening.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Overall, the facility is in need of a deep cleaning. Floors, walls, and ceilings throughout the facility were observed to be accumulated with soil and food debris. Countertops and shelves were filled with various items that were for personal use or items that were no longer usable. Be sure to organize and separate items that are going to be sold to the public versus items that are for personal use. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup and clutter throughout the facility.   

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed a container of personal food stored in the pizza dough cooler in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and food was removed from cooler. An employee stated that the container of food was recently placed inside of the cooler. Ensure that personal food items are always stored separate from food and drink items intended for public consumption.  

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.
